battle.name: 第三次敘利亞戰爭
battle.theater: 敘利亞濱海與赫勒斯滂海峽
battle.brief: 塞琉古二世與托勒密二世為敘利亞與赫勒斯滂海峽而開的第三次敘利亞戰爭，前252年開火，前245年以白銀賠款收場。埃及月牙劍此時已退出戰陣，只留在托勒密王朝的神廟與典禮中充當祖傳儀仗，實戰交由科皮斯與薩里薩方陣。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 第三次敘利亞戰爭是前3世紀中葉塞琉古王國與托勒密王國之間為敘利亞與愛琴海海峽而開的戰爭。塞琉古一方以安條克為王都，塞琉古二世卡利尼科斯自前261年即位，卻面對帝國三分的局面：母親貝勒尼基二世控制安條克與敘利亞，兄弟安條克·希埃拉克斯據亞細亞，另一兄弟腓力普守米底亞。塞琉古的野戰骨幹是安條克總督轄下的希臘化步兵與重裝車兵，王家常備的近衛亞革瑪是精銳的標槍騎兵；海防由帕特羅克勒斯率領的艦隊把守赫勒斯滂與博斯普魯斯的入口。托勒密一方以托勒密二世斐拉德夫斯為主，與妹妹兼妻子阿爾西諾二世共治，宮中由繼承人、將軍與幕僚構成決策核心；陸軍以馬其頓式方陣為骨幹，配以象兵與輕裝步兵，艦隊規模遠勝對手，並收編了腓尼基將領安德羅馬科斯與敘利亞的反抗派。捲入戰局的還有留居亞細亞的高盧傭兵，他們受埃及金錢煽動而叛離塞琉古，使希埃拉克斯無法回援本土。本戰的遠因也在希臘本土：前267年起的克里摩尼德戰爭中，安提柯二世貢納塔斯率馬其頓與伊庇魯斯的聯軍在海峽海戰中擊敗埃及艦隊，托勒密在希臘世界無法立足，才把力量北移至亞細亞。
countriesEn: The Third Syrian War was a conflict fought in the middle of the third century BC between the Seleucid Empire and the Ptolemaic Kingdom over Syria and the straits of the Aegean. On the Seleucid side the capital was Antioch, and Seleucus II Callinicus had held the throne since 261 BC, but he faced a three-way partition of the empire: his mother Berenice II held Antioch and Syria, his brother Antiochus Hierax occupied Asia Minor, and another brother, Philip, sat in Media. The backbone of the Seleucid field army was the Hellenistic infantry and heavy cavalry under the governor of Antioch, while the royal household guard, the agema, was an elite force of javelin-throwing riders; at sea the entrance to the Hellespont and the Bosporus was guarded by the fleet under Patrocles. The Ptolemaic side was led by Ptolemy II Philadelphus, who ruled jointly with his sister and wife Arsinoe II, with the heir apparent, the generals and the court forming the decision-making core. Its land army had the Macedonian phalanx as its backbone, supported by war elephants and light infantry, and its fleet was far larger than its opponent's; it also took over the Phoenician commander Andromachus and the Syrian opposition. Dragged into the war were the Gallic mercenaries who had settled in Asia Minor: bribed with Egyptian money they revolted from the Seleucids, which left Antiochus Hierax unable to come to the aid of the homeland. The deeper cause of the war lay in the Greek world as well: in the Chremonidean War, which began in 267 BC, Antigonus II Gonatas and the coalition of Macedon and Epirus defeated the Egyptian fleet at the straits, and with no foothold left in Greece, Ptolemy transferred his strength northward to Asia Minor.
people: 左右戰局的關鍵人物集中在塞琉古王室的內鬥與埃及的介入上。塞琉古二世卡利尼科斯是名義上的君主，他既要從母親貝勒尼基手中收回敘利亞，又要應付亞細亞的高盧傭兵，戰前曾打算用一場伏擊解決問題，最後只能靠賠款換取喘息。托勒密二世斐拉德夫斯是進攻的策動者，與妹妹兼妻子阿爾西諾二世共同執政，把海峽視為托勒密王國的命脈。貝勒尼基二世是安條克二世的王妃、塞琉古二世之母，前261年以安條克與敘利亞為基地迎埃及兵入城，終被兒子清除，傳說是毒殺。安條克·希埃拉克斯是亞細亞的統帥，曾在敘利亞擊敗托勒密支持的政敵，轉入亞細亞後卻在前255年前後兵敗於薩迪斯一帶的高盧傭兵，兵勢隨之瓦解。安德羅馬科斯是阿斯卡隆出身的腓尼基將領，叛投埃及後被托勒密任命為敘利亞沿海的統帥，約前245年死於己方或埃及方面的暗算。帕特羅克勒斯是塞琉古的海軍統帥，在赫勒斯滂一帶與埃及艦隊交戰失利，全軍隨風暴葬身大海。塞琉古的臣僕艾皮革涅斯曾勸王伏擊一艘載運重金的羅得島商船，想截下埃及付給高盧傭兵的金錢；羅得島人既不助塞琉古也不助埃及，而是把錢直接交給高盧人，這筆錢就此成了高盧叛亂的引爆點。史家波利比奧斯留下本戰最詳盡的記述，他本人當年也在希臘為抗馬其頓而周旋。
peopleEn: The people who decided the war cluster around the infighting in the Seleucid royal house and the intervention of Egypt. Seleucus II Callinicus was the monarch in name: he had to take Syria back from his mother Berenice and to deal with the Gallic mercenaries in Asia Minor, and before the war he even tried to settle the matter with a single ambush, ending up with nothing but an indemnity to buy breathing space. Ptolemy II Philadelphus was the man behind the offensive; ruling jointly with his sister and wife Arsinoe II, he treated the straits as the lifeline of the Ptolemaic kingdom. Berenice II, wife of Antiochus II and mother of Seleucus II, used Antioch and Syria as a base to bring Egyptian troops into the city in 261 BC, and was finally removed by her son, legend has it by poison. Antiochus Hierax commanded in Asia Minor: he had defeated the Ptolemaic-backed faction in Syria, but in Asia Minor his army was broken by the Gallic mercenaries around Sardis in about 255 BC, and his position disintegrated with it. Andromachus of Ascalon, a Phoenician officer who had served the Seleucids, defected to Egypt and was installed by Ptolemy II as commander of the Syrian coast; around 245 BC he was killed, either by his own men or by agents of the Egyptians. Patrocles was the Seleucid admiral; he lost a naval engagement against the Egyptian fleet off the Hellespont and his whole force went down in the storm. Epigenes, a minister of Seleucus, urged his king to ambush a Rhodian merchant ship carrying heavy gold in order to intercept the money the Egyptians were paying to the Gallic mercenaries; the Rhodians helped neither side but handed the money straight to the Gauls, and that payment became the trigger of the Gallic revolt. The most detailed account of the war comes from the historian Polybius, who in those same years was himself active in Greece in opposition to Macedon.
kits: 這場戰爭裡真正成列的兵器，已經不是卡牌上那把埃及月牙劍。月牙劍在前3世紀中葉的埃及是禮器而非戰具：托勒密王朝的神廟浮雕與王權圖像裡，索卡爾與奧西里斯常手執月牙劍，與象徵王權的權杖並列，祭司的行列也以它作為身份的標記；埃及軍中偶有沿用舊式外彎單刃刀者，但主力早已換成馬其頓傳入的科皮斯（彎刃單手刀）、短劍、薩里薩長矛與圓盾方陣，以及前3世紀仍稱雄的非洲象兵。托勒密方的投射武器是亞洲式複合弓與標槍，塞琉古方則有皮諾斯式鍍銀圓盾、狹長的特拉蒙式小盾，以及來自羅得島與南義大利的擲石手，騎兵使用長標槍與科皮斯。攻城與野戰器械方面，雙方都備有弩砲、投石機、攻城塔與壕溝器材；托勒密軍在海峽一線還依賴大型多列槳戰船與運輸快艇，控制海峽等於同時掐住黑海小麥輸送與商船通行稅。埃及的補給靠尼羅河穀物經海運與陸路接運，塞琉古則有安條克的儲糧與敘利亞內陸的道路網；高盧傭兵自備攻城器材，靠劫掠與突襲維生。
kitsEn: The weapons that actually formed up on the field in this war were no longer the Egyptian khopesh shown on the card. By the middle of the third century BC the khopesh was a ceremonial object in Egypt rather than a weapon: in the temple reliefs and royal images of the Ptolemaic kingdom, Sokar and Osiris are shown holding the khopesh alongside the staff that symbolises royal power, and processions of priests used it as a badge of rank. A few Egyptian soldiers still carried the old outward-curving single-edged blade, but the main body of the army had long since switched to the Macedonian kopis, the short sword, the sarissa and the round shield of the phalanx, together with the African elephants that were still the arm of choice in the third century BC. The Ptolemaic missile arm was the Asiatic composite bow and the javelin, while the Seleucids used the Pelta-type silvered round shield, the narrow telamon-type small shield, and slingers from Rhodes and southern Italy, their cavalry carrying the long kontos and the kopis. Both sides brought siege equipment into the field: bolt-shooting artillery, stone-throwers, siege towers and trenching gear. In the straits the Ptolemaic fleet depended on large many-oared ships and fast transports, and control of the straits meant a stranglehold at once on the Black Sea grain supply and on the tolls levied on passing merchantmen. Egypt drew its supply from the Nile's grain moved by sea and by road, the Seleucids from the stores of Antioch and the road network of the Syrian interior, while the Gallic mercenaries carried their own siege gear and lived off plunder and sudden raids.
tactics: 開戰的部署是典型的兩棲配合：托勒密以海軍先行切入赫勒斯滂與博斯普魯斯，奪取海峽兩岸的制水權，再以陸軍沿腓尼基與敘利亞海岸北上，企圖把安條克與奧龍特斯河谷收入囊中。塞琉古的應對不是正面決戰，而是依托奧龍特斯河與山地的險阻、據點防守，配以游擊與斷糧，同時用帕特羅克勒斯率領的艦隊扼住海峽通道，企圖在托勒密海軍立足未穩時將其逐出。前260年代艾皮革涅斯那場針對載金商船的伏擊計畫，說明雙方都動用金融手段而非會戰來決定戰局；羅得島人把金錢直接交給高盧傭兵，等於替埃及買下一批最難纏的戰兵。亞細亞方面，高盧傭兵以遊擊式的山地戰術襲擾城邑、切斷亞細亞與安條克之間的補給走廊，使希埃拉克斯的援軍無法和主力會師。野戰中，馬其頓式方陣的長矛牆與相互保護的協同是兩軍共有的骨架，車兵與重騎用於突破，輕步兵與投射兵在兩翼和側後展開；雙方在安條克平原與海岸據點間的反覆拉鋸，最終以海峽的實力消長定出勝負。塞琉古方面的致命顧慮是雙線作戰：一旦亞細亞失守，安條克方向的糧道與兵源都會被切斷。
tacticsEn: The deployment at the opening of the war was a classic combination of sea and land. Ptolemy moved his fleet first into the Hellespont and the Bosporus to seize the command of the water on both sides of the straits, then marched his land force north along the Phoenician and Syrian coast in the hope of enveloping Antioch and the Orontes valley. The Seleucid answer was not a set-piece battle: they relied on the natural obstacles of the Orontes and the hills, on fortified posts, on raids and on cutting supplies, while Patrocles' fleet held the entrance to the straits in the hope of driving the Ptolemaic navy out before it was firmly established. The plan of ambush against the gold-laden merchant ship devised in the 260s by Epigenes shows that both sides fought the war with financial instruments rather than with set-piece engagements; by handing the money directly to the Gallic mercenaries the Rhodians bought Egypt the most troublesome soldiers in the east. In Asia Minor the Gallic bands fought a guerrilla war in the hills, raiding towns and cutting the supply corridor between Asia Minor and Antioch, so that the relieving army of Antiochus Hierax could never join the main force. In the field the skeleton of both armies was the Macedonian phalanx, its wall of sarissas and its mutual support, with cavalry and heavy horse used for the breakthrough and light infantry and missile troops deployed on the flanks and in the rear. The repeated tug of war between the Antioch plain and the coastal strongholds was decided in the end by the shifting balance of power in the straits. The fatal Seleucid anxiety was fighting on two fronts: once Asia Minor was lost, the grain route and the man-power feeding Antioch from the east were cut as well.
data: 斷代方面，第三次敘利亞戰爭一般定在前252年至前245年，連同前261至前253年間托勒密二世與塞琉古二世的那一輪衝突，托勒密在敘利亞前後拉鋒近二十年。地理尺度上，赫勒斯滂海峽最窄處約一點二公里，博斯普魯斯海峽最窄處約七百公尺；由安條克沿海航行至赫勒斯滂約九百公里，至博斯普魯斯約一千一百公里。兵力的量級差是戰局的底色：史料在描述埃及方面的投入時以萬人為單位——步兵、騎兵、象兵與龐大艦隊同時上陣，而塞琉古在敘利亞能調集的野戰兵力以數千為主，海軍更只有帕特羅克勒斯那支以數十艘戰艦為限的艦隊。損失方面，海峽一役中帕特羅克勒斯率領的艦隊幾乎全滅，他本人與數十艘船一同葬身風暴；亞細亞方面，希埃拉克斯的軍隊在前255年前後亦被高盧人擊潰。結算方面，和約以白銀計價，數以萬計的塔蘭特分期支付，另有若干城邑與海峽據點的交還，戰費的負擔延續到托勒密二世去世之後。
dataEn: As to dating, the Third Syrian War is generally placed between 252 and 245 BC; taken together with the earlier round of fighting between Ptolemy II and Seleucus II in 261 to 253 BC, Ptolemy had been tugging at Syria for close on twenty years. The geography sets the scale: the narrowest point of the Hellespont is about 1.2 kilometres and that of the Bosporus about 700 metres; the sea route from Antioch to the Hellespont is some 900 kilometres and to the Bosporus about 1,100. The gap in the order of magnitude is the subtext of the whole campaign. When the sources describe the Egyptian commitment they speak in units of ten thousands, with infantry, cavalry, elephants and a huge fleet all deployed at once, whereas the Seleucids could muster in Syria field armies of a few thousand men, and at sea had only Patrocles' fleet of some dozens of warships. In terms of loss, Patrocles' fleet was virtually destroyed in the engagement in the straits, he himself perishing with dozens of ships in the storm, and in Asia Minor the army of Antiochus Hierax was likewise crushed by the Gauls around 255 BC. The settlement was priced in silver, with a number of tens of thousands of talents paid in instalments, together with the return of certain cities and positions in the straits, and the burden of the war outlived the death of Ptolemy II.
cause: 起因是多層的。安條克二世前260年陣亡於以弗所，塞琉古帝國隨即分崩：母親貝勒尼基二世握有安條克與敘利亞，兩位兄弟分別控制亞細亞與米底亞，王位繼承者塞琉古二世只握有正規軍與部分王都防務。托勒密二世以支持貝勒尼基、並在敘利亞扶植受其控制的官員為名，把敘利亞變成托勒密的前線。更深層的動機是海峽：控制赫勒斯滂與博斯普魯斯者，可以向過境船隊徵稅，可以截斷黑海輸入埃及的小麥供應，也可以壟斷愛琴海貿易；這是托勒密王朝自前3世紀初以來一貫的海峽政策，前267年的克里摩尼德戰爭中安提柯二世在海峽擊敗埃及海軍，正是這一政策受挫後托勒密把力量北移的直接理由。塞琉古二世則必須阻止托勒密控制安條克與奧龍特斯河谷這條南北陸路同地中海的接點。導火線是前260年代貝勒尼基被清算、敘利亞回歸塞琉古二世直轄之後，托勒密以敘利亞人受壓迫為由再啟戰端；亞細亞的高盧傭兵之亂則抽走了希埃拉克斯的援軍，使塞琉古無法兩面作戰，這一點在實際戰略上的分量，可能比海峽本身更重。
causeEn: The causes were layered. Antiochus II died at Ephesus in 260 BC and the Seleucid empire fell apart: his mother Berenice II held Antioch and Syria, two brothers respectively held Asia Minor and Media, and the heir, Seleucus II Callinicus, possessed only the regular army and part of the capital's defences. Ptolemy II moved under the pretext of supporting Berenice and of placing officials of his own choosing in Syria, which turned the province into a Ptolemaic front. The deeper motive was the straits: whoever held the Hellespont and the Bosporus could tax passing shipping, could cut off the Black Sea wheat on which Egypt depended, and could monopolise Aegean trade. This was the consistent policy of the Ptolemaic dynasty from the early third century BC, and the defeat inflicted on the Egyptian fleet in the straits by Antigonus II during the Chremonidean War of 267 BC was the direct reason why Ptolemy now threw his weight northward into Asia Minor. Seleucus II for his part had to prevent Ptolemy from holding Antioch and the Orontes valley, the point where the north-south land road met the Mediterranean. The spark was the liquidation of Berenice in the 260s and the return of Syria to Seleucus II's direct rule, after which Ptolemy once again invoked the oppression of the Syrians as his pretext. The revolt of the Gallic mercenaries in Asia Minor drained away the relieving army of Antiochus Hierax and left Seleucus unable to fight on two fronts, and in the actual strategy of the war that may have weighed more than the straits themselves.
impact: 本戰對塞琉古的代價主要在財政。塞琉古二世雖保住了安條克與敘利亞，卻在和約中支付了巨額白銀，國庫為之一空；此後二十餘年間塞琉古王室的銀幣成色明顯下降，正是戰費與歲出失控的直接後果。塞琉古宮廷的清洗也從此加劇，母親與兄弟相繼被除，安條克的朝堂在二十年間換了數批人。對托勒密而言，控制海峽的目標只在數年內實現：海峽一度由埃及與其盟友掌控，黑海小麥與通行稅一度改由亞歷山大里亞的商船經手，卻因賠款與亞細亞的牽制而未能把敘利亞變成埃及的屬地；塞浦路斯與愛琴海的島嶼則成為托勒密在愛琴海的永久基地。對武器制度的影響更為長遠：月牙劍在這一代人眼中已是神廟裡的祖傳禮器，與手杖、聖印並列，實戰的標準配置早已換成科皮斯、薩里薩與方陣盾，這說明埃及本土的冷兵器傳統在希臘化時期被馬其頓式軍備整體取代。塞琉古與托勒密在此後數十年維持脆弱的冷和平，直到前3世紀末托勒密四世與安條克四世之間的拉提亞戰爭才再度全面爆發。
impactEn: The chief cost of the war to the Seleucids was financial. Seleucus II kept Antioch and Syria, but the treaty drained the treasury of enormous sums of silver, and the visible decline in the silver content of Seleucid coinage over the following two decades or more is the direct consequence of war expenditure and runaway obligations. Purges in the Seleucid court also grew more frequent, with the mother and then the brothers removed in turn, and the Antioch court changing hands several times in twenty years. For the Ptolemies the aim of controlling the straits was realised only for a few years: the straits were at one point in Egyptian hands, Black Sea wheat and the passage tolls passed for a time through the merchantmen of Alexandria, yet neither the indemnity nor the entanglement in Asia Minor allowed Syria to be turned into a Ptolemaic possession; Cyprus and the Aegean islands, by contrast, became permanent Ptolemaic bases in the Aegean. The effect on the arms themselves was the more lasting: by this generation the khopesh was a hereditary object of ritual in the temples, ranged alongside the staff and the seal, while the standard battlefield kit had long since become the kopis, the sarissa and the shield of the phalanx. This shows how thoroughly the indigenous Egyptian tradition of cutting weapons was displaced by Macedonian-style equipment in the Hellenistic age. Between them, Seleucids and Ptolemies then maintained a fragile armed peace for several decades, until the Laodicean War between Ptolemy IV and Antiochus IV at the close of the third century BC broke out in full once more.
result: 打完了。托勒密二世未能攻下安條克，也沒能把塞琉古逐出敘利亞；塞琉古二世同樣沒能把埃及逐出海峽。約前245年，在托勒密二世病逝、其子托勒密三世歐厄革忒斯即位之後，雙方以白銀賠款與據點交還議和：托勒密方面撤出赫勒斯滂與博斯普魯斯的駐軍，塞琉古方面則分期支付賠款，結束了這場長達七年的消耗。塞琉古保住了安條克、奧龍特斯河谷與敘利亞內陸的完整，也保住了安條克以東的王室土地；代價是財政空虛與貨幣成色下降，以及希埃拉克斯兵敗之後亞細亞的失血。托勒密得到的是海峽的暫時勝利與愛琴海的基地，一個沒有安條克的敘利亞，以及一條被暫時掐斷又重新打開的海上通道。亞細亞的收場最為慘烈：高盧傭兵攻佔薩迪斯，安條克·希埃拉克斯兵敗逃亡，希臘化帝國在東方的內鬥因此進一步惡化。此後近四分之一個世紀，兩大強權再未在敘利亞正面開火。
resultEn: It was over. Ptolemy II had not taken Antioch, nor had he driven the Seleucids out of Syria, and Seleucus II had not driven the Egyptians out of the straits. Around 245 BC, after the death of Ptolemy II and the accession of his son Ptolemy III Euergetes, the two sides came to terms: an indemnity in silver and the return of positions, the Ptolemies withdrawing their garrisons from the Hellespont and the Bosporus while the Seleucids paid the indemnity in instalments, which closed a war of attrition that had run for seven years. The Seleucids kept Antioch, the Orontes valley and the Syrian interior intact, and kept the royal lands east of the capital; the price was an empty treasury, thinner silver in the coinage, and the bleeding of Asia Minor after the defeat of Antiochus Hierax. The Ptolemies gained a short-lived mastery of the straits and a set of Aegean bases, a Syria without Antioch, and a sea route pinched shut and then reopened. The worst ending was in Asia Minor, where the Gallic mercenaries took Sardis, Antiochus Hierax was routed and fled, and the civil war inside the Hellenistic empire in the east grew worse in consequence. For close on a quarter of a century afterwards the two great powers did not once fight openly over Syria again.
